clue.text: Bring up fine record in sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade and penalty abbreviation for fine
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone raising a fine for a sporting record.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs on a course.

clue.text: Race injury

definitions.meaning: a ... is a breed or lineage, as a ... of a species
a pulled muscle or overstretched ligament

explanation.surface: A runner hurt during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain names both a lineage within a species and a muscle injury from overstretching.

clue.text: Gone with mentor to travel around country

indicators.note: letters that travel around move about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has left with their mentor for a tour of a foreign land.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a Balkan nation on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Go round part of theatre

definitions.meaning: to move around something in a loop
the dress ... or upper ... is a tier of seating in a theatre

explanation.surface: An instruction to walk round a section of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Circle is a verb for orbiting something and a noun for a raised seating tier in theatres.

clue.text: Colour that is away from cue ball

parts.note: off means away from, as in 'off the coast'
in snooker and pool the cue ball is the white

explanation.surface: A snooker player's ball has rolled away from the white, describing a shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-white is a pale shade, white tinged with grey or yellow.

clue.text: Somewhat unbearable horse

indicators.note: somewhat signals only some of the word is used, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A horse that is a bit hard to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse noted for speed and stamina.

clue.text: Memorable broadcast expressed disapproval of Ian Fleming's Goldfinger

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the phrase is judged by sound

parts.words: expressed disapproval of Ian Fleming's Goldfinger
parts.note: hissed means expressed disapproval, and Auric is the first name of Fleming's villain Goldfinger

explanation.surface: A notable radio programme in which someone booed the Bond villain Goldfinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' asks you to say HISSED AURIC aloud; it runs together as HISTORIC. Auric Goldfinger is the title villain of Ian Fleming's James Bond novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic event is one important enough to be remembered.

clue.text: Geordie Mark discovered gadgets giving close shaves

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Tyneside in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: discovered here means uncovered, with the outer letters stripped off

parts.note: things is a loose word for gadgets or objects

explanation.surface: A man from Newcastle called Mark found razors that give a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the first and last letters from Mark, leaving AR. A Geordie is someone from Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a narrow escape, just as a close shave is.

clue.text: Whip dismissed by party

parts.note: a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A political whip sacked by their own party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like a parliamentary officer but is the verb meaning to beat. OUT is a cricket term: a dismissed batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip a rival in a contest is to beat them comprehensively, to outdo them.

clue.text: Conclude letter on Scrabble board will be unproductive

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
each letter in Scrabble is a small tile placed on the board

explanation.surface: Deciding that a particular letter placed in Scrabble will score nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Infertile land or livestock yields no crops or offspring, so it is barren.

clue.text: Wild time getting half-cut in Swiss capital

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the currency name, splitting it open

parts.note: capital here is money, and the franc is the Swiss currency

indicators.note: cut in half, so only the first half of the word time is used

explanation.surface: Someone having a riotous, half-drunk time in Bern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swiss capital' wants to be Bern; it is the currency, the franc. 'half-cut' keeps TI from 'time', which goes 'in' FRANC. Half-cut is also British slang for tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and wild both describe behaviour that is frenzied and out of control.

clue.text: Lexicographer, internet celebrity releasing article for magazine finally

parts.note: the web is the internet

indicators.note: releasing one letter for another means letting it go and putting a replacement in its place

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word magazine

explanation.surface: An online celebrity who writes dictionaries, mentioned at the end of a magazine article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing ... for' swaps the A of STAR for E, the last letter of 'magazine', giving STER.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah Webster compiled the American dictionary that still carries his name.

clue.text: Cleric, head of chapter soon

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of chapter

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A clergyman expected to become head of the cathedral chapter shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral.

clue.text: International limits designed to protect American economic system

parts.note: an international player is one awarded a cap for representing their country

indicators.note: one part protects another by surrounding it
designed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: International trade limits drawn up to shield an American market system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' is a player capped for their country, a British sporting usage. 'designed' signals the anagram and 'to protect' the wrap round the American letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalism is an economic order based on private ownership and markets.

clue.text: City journalist, essentially stingy, rejected hot food

parts.note: ed is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, the middle letters of stingy
rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted reporter sending back a hot meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the core of 'stingy'; 'rejected' turns the hot food round into BURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland.

clue.text: Chef Raymond overcoming skin complaint to provide dessert

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits on top of it

parts.note: Raymond Blanc is a French chef famous in Britain
mange is a skin disease of animals causing hair loss

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef beating a rash to serve a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Blanc is a French chef well known on British television. In a down clue 'overcoming' sets BLANC above MANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Blancmange is a sweet set milk pudding served as a dessert.

clue.text: Bird damaged rear fencing pole

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird has broken the back post of a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a bird of prey, famous for its diving speed.

clue.text: Backlash from Establishment after Conservative's demotion

indicators.note: a demotion sends someone lower, so the letter moves further down the word

parts.note: creation means establishment, the act of founding something
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Public backlash from the political Establishment after a Tory is demoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demotion' moves the C of CREATION down the word, giving REACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is a response against something, as a backlash is.

clue.text: He possibly is angriest when drunk

definitions.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, one example of the answer

indicators.note: drunk suggests reeling about, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who becomes most aggressive after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man but is helium; 'possibly' says it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is a noble gas that barely reacts with anything.

clue.text: Get into debt surrounded by latest fancy kitchen items

indicators.note: one piece surrounded by another sits inside it
fancy signals the letters are fancifully rearranged

parts.note: to owe is to be in debt

explanation.surface: Borrowing money to buy the newest designer kitchen gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reshuffles the word to TEATLS, and 'surrounded by' puts the debt word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea towels are cloths used in a kitchen to dry washed dishes.

clue.text: Religious belief almost undermining star, oddly

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece undermining another sits beneath it
oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of star
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a credo is a statement of belief

explanation.surface: A faith nearly bringing down a celebrity in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts CREDO to CRED; 'oddly' takes SA from 'star'; 'undermining' puts CRED under SA in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred describes what is holy or connected with religion.

clue.text: Group embraces, quietly departing

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so this letter is removed

parts.note: clasps means embraces or holds tightly
p, piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A group of people hug one another and then leave without a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a set or category of things sharing a quality.

clue.text: Question worker sceptically

parts.note: to ask is to question
the ant is the stock crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Interrogating an employee with doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking askant, an old variant of askance, is eyeing something with suspicion.

clue.text: Releases yob that keeps drug stash regularly hidden

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the other letters go inside
hidden reinforces that the drug letters are tucked inside the yob

parts.note: a lout is a yob, a rough uncouth youth
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of stash

explanation.surface: A thug who keeps his drugs out of sight is let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes TS from 'stash'; with E that makes ETS, which LOUT 'keeps hidden'.
explanation.definitionFit: To let out a prisoner or animal is to set it free, releasing it.

clue.text: Sign of females losing weight

indicators.note: losing a letter means it is dropped from the word

parts.note: women are females

explanation.surface: An indication of women dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Code-breaker, person of exceptional ability

definitions.meaning: someone who cracks codes or passwords
informally an outstanding person or thing

explanation.surface: A cryptanalyst described as brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracker means one who breaks into codes and, colloquially, someone first-rate.

clue.text: Reportedly true length of film

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: Reports say a film's running time is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a spool of film, and so a measure of footage.

clue.text: Shop introduces additional area for pottery

indicators.note: a word that introduces others takes them inside itself

parts.note: a store is a shop
new means additional, as in new members

explanation.surface: A shop opens an extra section for ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' means the shop takes the other two pieces inside it; 'additional' fits new as in 'new recruits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoneware is a dense kind of fired ceramic ware.

clue.text: Image created from brass rubbing?

parts.note: a brass rubbing copies a church brass, but rubbing a brass lamp as Aladdin did summons a magical spirit

explanation.walkthrough: A brass rubbing is paper rubbed over a church memorial brass to copy its picture; here the brass rubbed is Aladdin's lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Aladdin story, a spirit appears when the lamp is rubbed.
